subject: Re: MAP & POC network ownership — Redwood <> ClearSight
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <a.rivera@clearsighthealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: MAP kickoff: POC environment ownership and network items

Alex — following up from our call this morning. Thanks for outlining the POC criteria; to make the MAP explicit we put together a short ownership checklist for the environment pieces you flagged. Attached is the draft MAP (MAP_v1_Clearsight_Redwood.pdf). Key asks from our side: 

- Org + API keys: Redwood will create the service account and initial API keys if you prefer us to issue them; alternatively, you can create under your org and we will validate. Owner: ClearSight (prod-owner) or Redwood (temp) — please confirm.
- IP allowlist: we need a list of egress IPs for your firewall. We can provide static egress IPs from our Dedicated pool or use VPC peering and private IPs. Attachment: network_requirements.xlsx includes expected IP ranges.
- VPC peering: if you want traffic fully private we recommend VPC peering (preferred for PHI workloads). We need: project IDs, CIDR ranges we should avoid, and a peering window you'd like to schedule.
- Credentials handoff: redwood_server_key_instructions.txt lists required key rotation cadence and where keys live.

Can you confirm: (1) who will create the Redwood org entry (ClearSight IT or Redwood SRE), (2) whether you want public IP allowlisting or VPC peering, and (3) a target week for the peering window (we can support 12/7–12/11 PST).

If it's helpful I'll schedule a 30-min technical handoff next week with Grace and Jonas to walk the network sheet and share the minimal ACLs.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Alex Rivera <a.rivera@clearsighthealth.com>

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: POC environment ownership and network items

Marcus — thanks, received and we looked over the MAP doc. Quick responses inline: 

- Org + API keys: ClearSight prefers to own the org entry for security reasons. IT will create a service account and send you the details. Owner: ClearSight IT (we will share an admin to validate).
- IP allowlist vs peering: for the POC we want private traffic; VPC peering is preferred. We can do a peering for the POC subnet only.
- Peering window: 12/8 or 12/9 works best for our network team.

I'll loop in Chris (network lead) and procurement on the next steps — procurement will need the statement of work and the short-term demo credits in the MAP for budgeting. Alex
